title: Econ lifecycle sprint-gate for batching/caching/quantization
creator: Aisha Mehta
description: Objective: Build a gated, repeatable sprint process (the 'Sprint-Gate') to validate incremental cost-saving levers—specifically batching heuristics, prefix/KV caching policies, and quantization profiles—while preventing quality regressions for production workloads. This ticket coordinates the PM-level roadmap, success metrics, experiment gates, and cross-functional handoffs required to run a 6-week incremental rollout across Hosted API customers and Dedicated pools. The Sprint-Gate approach: 1) Hypothesis + safety criteria, 2) Controlled experiment (A/B or route-level canary) with telemetry and quality checks, 3) Gate review (PM/Research/Eng/SRE) for expansion, 4) Phased rollout with rollback triggers and guardrails. This artifact centralizes milestones, acceptance criteria, queryables, and stakeholder commitments for the program.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Each cost lever has at least one controlled experiment pipeline instrumented against production traffic with pre/post evaluation metrics.
A2: Rollout gates defined with clear pass/fail thresholds (quality, latency, error rates, cost delta) and automated rollback hooks.
A3: Telemetry dashboards and alerting created for token-econ, tail-latency, and hallucination signal coverage.
A4: Post-rollout regression tests and a 2-week monitoring window with documented runbook for incidents.
A5: Cross-functional sign-off recorded in this ticket before any broad customer expansion.

metrics: Token-cost delta (per-1M tokens) target: -12% baseline after first-wave optimizations
Tail latency P99: no more than +5% relative to baseline during canary
Quality guardrail: automated eval suite pass rate >= 98% on monitored prompt set
Adoption: 20% of eligible routes moved to optimized profile within 2 weeks of gate
Rollback sensitivity: any model-level hallucination increase > 1.5x triggers immediate rollback
stakeholders: Design/UX: Priya Nair (console UX for rollout controls)
risks_mitigation: Risk: Quality regressions in long-tail prompts — Mitigation: maintain controlled A/B on seeded traffic and expand eval prompt set; automatic rollback if eval score drops below threshold.
Risk: Telemetry blind spots — Mitigation: deploy additional sampling instrumentation and synthetic traffic generators before canary.
Risk: Dedicated pools capacity mismatch — Mitigation: coordination ticket with infra for reserved capacity and throttling policies.
Risk: Customer surprise due to change in token accounting — Mitigation: pre-rollout customer comms and opt-out route flagging.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): Local experiments and offline evals; bench with synthetic traffic
Phase 1 (canary): 1% traffic on non-critical routes; heavy telemetry; 72h hold
Phase 2 (limited expansion): 10% traffic on targeted route classes with manual gate review
Phase 3 (broad expansion): automated rollout to eligible routes with monitoring guards and 2-week watch
Rollback: automated rollback on metric thresholds + manual rollback for unanticipated quality degradation
